items.line: Steps 1 to 4 run only when the import has both dates and is a person... 1. The name and, for "Surname, Forename", its flipped form, with both years exact. ... 3. The same names among `alternate_names`, on a candidate with both years exact. 4. The surname, on a candidate with both years exact.
items.requirement: find_entity must attempt resolution in priority order: name with birth/death dates, alternate_names with dates, surname with dates

items.line: 1. The name and, for "Surname, Forename", its flipped form, with both years exact. 2. The same names with today's tolerant date rule
items.requirement: When both birth_date and death_date are present they disambiguate records, and an exact year match for both takes precedence

items.line: Otherwise there is a single step, the name and its flipped form alone.
items.requirement: When either date is absent, fall back to case-insensitive name matching alone and return an existing record if one exists

items.line: **Given** the stored authors, **When** an import sends "WILLIAM H. BREWER" born "1829" died "1910", **Then** `find_entity` returns OL2A, the lowest numeric key, not OL10A.
items.requirement: Matching must be case-insensitive; different casings resolve to the same author record

items.line: **When** an import sends "Zed*" born "1829" died "1910", **Then** `import_author` returns a new candidate with the name "Zed*", born "1829", died "1910".
items.requirement: Support wildcards in name patterns; "John*" returns first candidate by numeric key; if none, a new candidate preserving the name including *

items.line: The same names among `alternate_names`, on a candidate with both years exact.
items.requirement: Alternate_names match requires both birth_date and death_date present and exactly matching the candidate's values

items.line: **When** an import sends "Mr. Harry J. Brewer" born "1829" with no death date, **Then** `find_entity` returns `None`.
items.requirement: Surname match requires both dates present and exactly matching; must not resolve if either is missing or mismatched

items.line: `import_author` returns a new candidate with the name "William H. Brewer", born "1829", died "1912".
items.requirement: If no valid match, return a new author candidate dict preserving name, birth_date, death_date unchanged

items.line: It owns the year rule: both sides have a four-digit year, found with `re_year`, and they are equal.
items.requirement: Year comparison considers only the year component; any year difference invalidates a match

items.line: **`find_entity(author)`** returns the first candidate of `find_author`, or `None`.
items.requirement: find_author(author) accepts the import dict and returns list of candidates; find_entity delegates to find_author and returns an existing record or None

items.line: It first removes every `_` from `pattern`, then `*` matches any run of characters, and every other character is literal.
items.requirement: Mock query behavior replicates production ILIKE semantics: case-insensitive full-string, * multi-char wildcard, _ ignored in patterns
